Subject: Re: Activation acceptance: smoke sweep, routing sanity, and runbook signoff

Hi Neha / Laura,

We're scheduled for the traffic flip on Thursday 2027-06-10. Before we confirm the go decision we need a short, evidence-backed acceptance: 1) confirmation KV cache priming completed, 2) a short smoke sweep across three core payment flows (auth, settle, refund), 3) routing sanity check for private-peering (ASN/SDN) and fallback to public egress.

Can you share an abbreviated runbook and expected time window for the smoke? We have engineers on standby and can do a canary at 10% traffic.

Thanks,
Sam
Operations Lead — Acme Payments

Attachment: acme-risk-summary-0506.pdf (attachment stub)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation acceptance: smoke sweep, routing sanity, and runbook signoff

Sam —

Thanks for the note. We're proposing the following lightweight acceptance flow (30–45m):
- Pre-check (15m): runbook checklist + KV cache priming evidence upload.
- Canary smoke (15m): 10% traffic, run auth/settle/refund scenarios, capture end-to-end traces.
- Routing sanity (10m): confirm private peering path + failover exercise to public egress.

Karthik is prepared to execute the runbook and will post results to the shared Drive link. After the canary, if error-rate <= 0.5% and tail p95 latency within our baseline, we can sign off for the broader flip.

I'm attaching the trimmed runbook and the KV checklist. Can you confirm an acceptable window (we're proposing Thu 2027-06-10 09:00–10:00 PT)?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior TPM, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Adding the execution plan and quick failure-cases we rehearsed:
1) KV priming: run warmup script (kv-warmup.sh) with prefix set 0001-0500, verify artifact smoke-run-report-*.csv exists, and sample cache hit rate >= 92%.
2) Canary smoke: run three scenario scripts (auth_flow.py, settle_flow.py, refund_flow.py) against canary endpoints. Monitor token-level latency and error-rate. If any scenario fails > 0.5% / 3m window, abort and escalate to the bridge.
3) Routing sanity: BGP path validation (show ip bgp summary) + SDN flow trace. Simulate failover by toggling secondary route on the router (config snippet in runbook).

I'll own step 1 & 2. Marissa will coordinate ops bridge. Mina will collect traces and upload zipped evidence to the Drive link.

-Karthik
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation acceptance: smoke sweep, routing sanity, and runbook signoff

Post-canary quick update:
- KV priming: complete. Sample hit rate 94.1%. Evidence uploaded: smoke-run-report-20270610.csv (Drive).
- Canary (10%): auth OK (0.12% err), settle OK (0.09% err), refund borderline (0.66% err) — caused by a transient downstream timeout at our gateway proxy. We throttled and retried; overall tail latency p95 within baseline.
- Routing sanity: BGP path confirmed; failover toggled and recovered within expected 6s.

Recommendation: Hold on full flip until we mitigate refund friction (engineer assigned) or accept a targeted retry policy for refund calls for the first 24h. Sam — advise whether Acme wants a hard hold or to proceed with mitigation in place.

-Karthik

Attachments: smoke-run-report-20270610.csv

From: samuel.cho@acme-payments.com

Thanks for the evidence. Acme accepts a targeted mitigation: proceed with flip but implement the retry policy and hold increased monitoring for 24h. We'll sign the acceptance note after we receive the final smoke PDF and the runbook change log.

Sam
